patch.value: Windows published-release verifier test can preempt its own readiness and cleanup contract

Merged-main CI run 33867283305 intermittently killed the published HTTP evaluator after 10 seconds while the evaluator contract permits 15 seconds of readiness plus 2 seconds of cleanup. spawnSync then returned a nonzero/null result with empty stderr, hiding whether discovery or cleanup failed. The exact failed job reran green, proving nondeterminism on byte-identical source rather than resolving the invalid timeout ordering.

The test-specific evaluator readiness bound is lower than the outer process timeout by at least the full shutdown grace; timeout arithmetic is asserted explicitly; the expected invalid-discovery path and port-reuse cleanup remain required; focused, full coverage, static, and hosted Windows gates pass.
Make the Windows published-artifact regression fail only on verifier behavior and always preserve a diagnostic before the harness deadline
Merged-main release readiness becomes deterministic and actionable instead of depending on hosted runner timing
Prevents false red release blockers and silent empty-stderr terminations in the Windows oracle
